subject: make one alone legend in ggplot2

messages.author: 4c1108aaddb5744d
messages.subject: make one alone legend in ggplot2
parts:
I have another question about plotting. when making time series plots, I have many variables in one figure, so a legend is necessary to read the plot. But then I use grid.arrange() to put them in one figure. Is there a way to make a stand alone legend that takes the position of one figure? Thanks.

df

year  month  A   B   C   D  E
2001      1     2   4    3   1   2
2001      2     3   1    2   3   3
2001      3     1   2    3   4   1
2001      4     2   2    3   5   3
....
2002
...

p2001 = ggplot()+
 geom_point(data=subset(df,year==2001), aes(x=month,y=A,colour='col a')+
 geom_point(data=subset(df,year==2001), aes(x=month,y=B,colour='col b')+
 geom_point(data=subset(df,year==2001), aes(x=month,y=C,colour='col c')+
scale_color_manual('',limits=c('col a','col b','col c'),values=c('red','green','yellow')
show(p2001)

then p2002 is subset of 2002.

grid.arrange(p2001,p2002,p2003,ncol=2)

I meant, is it possible to disable the legend in each figure, but have a common, separate legend takes the position of one plot, so there are four figures in one image? that way, it would be readable, because i have more variables than 3.

messages.author: 0c39e60ddb38622b
messages.subject: Re: make one alone legend in ggplot2
parts:
Try faceting by year - gridExtra isn't necessary. You should also put
the responses in long form using the reshape2 (or tidyr) packages.
Assuming A-E comprise all of your responses, something like (untested)

library(reshape2)
DFm <- melt(df, id = c("year", "month")) # stacks A-E into two columns

ggplot(DFm, aes(x = month, y = value, color = variable)) +
geom_path() + geom_point() +
scale_colour_brewer(palette = "Set 1") + # see
colorbrewer2.org for valid palettes
facet_wrap(~ year)

If you only want responses A-C (as in your example), then replace the
melt() call above with

DFm <- melt(df, id = c("year", "month"), measure = c("A", "B", "C"))

If the responses vary by year (which was not indicated, either in your
description or in your data), you should still be able to get the
above to work. If not, please provide a *reproducible* example (i.e.,
code + data in dput() form) in your next reply.

Dennis
